reflection.self_critique: The initial audit treated symptoms rather than systemic architecture failures. I missed that the lack of ROS lifecycle management guarantees zombie processes and memory leaks during long deployments, turning a 'FAIL' into an inevitable system crash after hours of operation. I was too lenient on dependency pinning by framing unpinned scipy as a 'risk' instead of an immediate runtime blocker in modern Python environments. I overlooked network security entirely; broadcasting control commands over unencrypted ROS topics is a critical attack vector. Regarding YOLO, I failed to address motion-blur degradation at high speeds and ignored class-imbalance bias that systematically suppresses low-confidence detections for rare hazards. Octo-models/octo handles these superiorly by employing learned safety priors through action chunking, built-in uncertainty quantification for perception fallbacks, standardized data versioning pipelines, and a modular policy architecture that decouples perception from control loops, enabling graceful degradation rather than hard failures.
missed_risks: Absence of ROS node lifecycle management and zombie process cleanup on abrupt termination
No graceful degradation or safe-stop fallback when Motive polling drops below 20Hz or YOLO inference stalls
Unencrypted ROS topic communication exposing control commands to network sniffing and spoofing
Missing motion-blur compensation in perception pipeline during high-velocity traversal
Hardcoded absolute paths preventing containerized deployment and cross-platform reproducibility
reflection.yolo_fix: Implement adaptive per-class confidence thresholding with dynamic lighting normalization (CLAHE + histogram equalization), integrate temporal tracking (ByteTrack) to filter transient shadow false positives, add motion-blur deconvolution preprocessing, retrain with balanced focal loss on low-contrast debris datasets, and deploy a lightweight uncertainty estimator (MC Dropout variance) to trigger safe-stop when detection confidence drops below 0.65 in unstructured terrain.
evolved_dimensions: Graceful degradation protocols and safe-stop fallback triggers under sensor dropout conditions
ROS lifecycle management with atomic shutdown hooks and zombie process reaping
Perception uncertainty quantification and dynamic threshold adaptation for environmental variance
Network security hardening including topic encryption, authentication, and rate-limiting
Containerized deployment reproducibility with absolute path resolution and environment variable injection

critical_flaws: Hardcoded robot IP (192.168.12.20) and ROS port prevent dynamic network adaptation and introduce single-point-of-failure risks
Missing explicit velocity/acceleration safety bounds enforcement despite ACCEL_SMOOTHING_ALPHA configuration
No hardware timestamp synchronization or PTP/NTP alignment logic for Motive-ROS sensor fusion
Unpinned scipy dependency creates high risk of AttributeError: module 'scipy.linalg' has no attribute 'tril' on newer environments
CrashLogger lacks atomic file writes and session state checkpointing, risking data corruption during abrupt power loss
yolo_errors: False positive classification of dynamic shadows as physical obstacles under direct sunlight
Missed detection of low-contrast ground debris due to insufficient small-object anchor scaling
Class confusion between navigable gravel and hazardous loose terrain in unstructured environments
obstacle_gaps: Blind spot coverage during rapid yaw maneuvers exceeding the 0.05s Motive polling interval
Failure to register transparent or highly reflective barriers without LiDAR/ultrasonic fallback
Position drift accumulation causing missed close-proximity obstacles when SLAM relocalization lags >200ms
